title: Monthly Streamflow Forecasting for the Naryn River Using XGBoost and SHAP Interpretability Based on Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data
content: Accurate monthly streamflow forecasting is essential for hydropower scheduling, irrigation planning, and flood preparedness in Central Asia. The Naryn River, the principal tributary feeding the Toktogul Reservoir, supplies over 40% of Kyrgyzstan’s electricity, yet conventional hydrological modelling of this basin is constrained by the scarcity of ground-based instrumentation at high elevations. This study develops an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting monthly discharge at the Toktogul inlet (41.83°N, 72.82°E) using exclusively open-access satellite and reanalysis products spanning January 2004 to March 2026. Seven data sources—ERA5-Land climate and hydrology variables, GloFAS v4.0 discharge reanalysis (target variable), GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage anomalies, the ENSO Oceanic Niño Index, and MODIS snow water equivalent—were integrated into a unified dataset of 263 monthly records. An XGBoost regression model was trained on 20 input features, refined from an initial pool of 22 candidates through backward elimination, with hyperparameters optimised via Optuna over 200 trials. A strict chronological train–test split (training: pre-2021; testing: 2021–2026) ensured temporal integrity. The model achieved NSE = 0.816, R2 = 0.816, MAE = 18.6 m3/s, and RMSE = 31.1 m3/s on the held-out test set, representing a 37% RMSE improvement over the persistence baseline. Five-fold time-series cross-validation yielded R2 = 0.875 ± 0.068, outperforming Random Forest (0.796 ± 0.065) and confirming superior generalisation. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis identified lagged discharge, temperature, and rolling precipitation averages as the dominant predictors, consistent with the snow-dominated hydrological regime. Seasonal error analysis revealed strong winter accuracy (MAE = 3.7 m3/s) but elevated summer errors (MAE = 45.8 m3/s), attributable to unrepresented glacier melt processes. The proposed framework constitutes a reproducible, satellite-driven pipeline transferable to other ungauged mountain basins in the region.
